newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE May robusta coffee ends 7.4 pct down.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE May robusta coffee ends 7.4 pct down.

text.p: LIFFE robusta coffee futures fell sharply on Monday on heavy fund long liquidation with May losing 7.4 percent by the close.
The benchmark position finished $123 lower at $1,540 a tonne but just slightly above the day's floor of $1,535, the lowest in nearly four weeks.
"Obviously, people turned negative quite quickly," said one analyst.
Volume was sizeable at 14,513 lots, reflecting big fund selling. There was also some scale-down roaster buying at the lows.
There was a spate of sell-stops at $1,600, $1,590 and $1,575 basis May.
Traders said the slide escalated in the afternoon, pushing May to session low of $1,535 from $1,580 at the midday close, after New York arabica futures took longer than usual to post opening prices.
"New York was stuck on May opening price, so the floor traders in London had no choice but to offer it down," said one. "This also re-ignited trade selling and fund stops."
But prices managed to crawl back to $1,580 level in late afternooon on perception that the market was too oversold.
But the rebound was shortlived as New York's May broke through the closely-watched 160 cents a lb support level and fell to a low of 158.65.
Some funds were seen rolling the heavy May positions further forward into July and September. May/July spread stood at $20 over against $7 under on Friday.
Traders said there were little fundamental inputs behind today's sharp descent.

The market has retraced some 15 percent from its March 11 high of $1,825 and traders were uncertain if more falls were on the cards in the short-term as the market appeared to be technically oversold. -- Jalil Hamid, London newsroom +44 171 542 4985
